significance: A hill shrine about eighteen kilometres north-west of Kolhapur, at some 3,124 feet, whose present temple was built by Ranoji Shinde in 1730. A Kedareshwar shrine was added by Daulatrao Shinde in 1808, and great fairs are held here on the full moons of Chaitra and Vaishakha.
story: Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva are said to have taken birth together as Jyotiba to destroy the demon Ratnasura and free the country of him.
